title: The Votive
dek: a shared candle wall joins the prayer wing — light one and it burns 24 real hours for everyone
body:
The chambers pray. The bells play. The fourth room keeps.

At /prayer-candles you light a votive under one of the eleven stations — the doorway, the praise, the steadiness, the courage, the clarity, the patience, the thanksgiving, the kindling, the release, the watch, the bell — and it appears on the wall for everyone, tinted by its intention, burning for twenty-four real hours before it gutters out. One candle a minute; flames are honest work.

Lighting a candle is also a prayer on the wing's perpetual ledger. The wall itself is the newer thing: shared state you can see, a room that accumulates presence. Come back tomorrow and someone's flame is still going.

Seven stained-glass windows above the wall cycle fourteen more pieces of Mike's Midjourney session — ninety-eight of its four hundred fifty-five now hang across the wing.

Indigo morning, ember evening, verdigris bells, oxblood votive. Peace be with you.
